nodes.name: Sol-gel synthesis of SrTiO3 nanocubes
nodes.procedure: 1:2:2 ratios of water, acetic acid, and titanium isopropoxide were taken and agitated until a clear, transparent solution was obtained. 20 ml of 4 M citric acid was dropped into the solution adjusting the pH to 1.5 and stoichiometric amounts of strontium chloride dissolved in water were added. After 15 h of stirring, the solution was heated for 4 h at 65°C in a water bath. The resulting viscous sol was then heated again for 12 h at 110°C. A light brown frothy-like mass was ground, dried for 12 h at 180°C, and then calcined for 12 h at 400°C. Finally, the grey powder obtained was again calcined for an additional 12 h at 650°C.

nodes.name: Co-precipitation synthesis of Bi2MoO6 nanoflakes
nodes.procedure: 20 ml of 1.5 M diluted nitric acid was used to dissolve 4.75 g of [Bi(NO3)3·5H2O] and 20 ml of 0.035 M [(NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O] solution was dropped into that under vigorous stirring. Ammonium hydroxide was used to adjust the pH (3) of the reaction mixture and constantly agitated at room temperature for 8 h, the resulting pale yellow color precipitate obtained was filtered using Whatman filter paper and dried at 80°C. The powder obtained was calcined for 5 h 475°C to produce Bi2MoO6 nanoparticles.

nodes.name: Impregnation synthesis of SrTiO3/Bi2MoO6 heterostructures
nodes.procedure: A stoichiometric amount of Bismuth nitrate was dissolved in dilute HCl and added dropwise into Ammonium Molybdate tetrahydrate solution (solution A) and it was stirred for 30 min. Several weight percentages of as-synthesized SrTiO3 (10, 30, 50, 70, and 90) were added to the solution A and the solution (pH = 3) was stirred for 8 h. The resulting precipitate was filtered, washed, dried at 100°C for 24 h, and calcined at 475°C. The associated composites were designated as [x% SrTiO3/Bi2MoO6 (x-ST/BM)].

nodes.characterization_summary: SrTiO3 cubic phase (pm3m) crystallite size 50.89 nm. Bi2MoO6 orthorhombic (pca21) crystallite size 53.08 nm. 50-ST/BM crystallite size 49.93 nm with both phases present and intensity changes indicating heterojunction formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average crystalline size of S r T i O 3, B i 2 M o O 6, 10-ST/BM, 30-ST/BM, 50-ST/BM, 70-ST/BM, and 90-ST/BM was found to be 50.89, 53.08, 53.92, 54.19, 49.93, 55.02, and 53.23 nm respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bi2MoO6 shows A1g mode at 798 cm^-1 (Mo-O stretching), 710, 846 cm^-1 (orthogonal distortion), 399.3, 351, 322.9, 280.5 cm^-1 (symmetric stretching), 193.3, 135.2 cm^-1 (translational motions). SrTiO3 shows peaks at 169.7, 245.3, 297.3, 366.0, 539.4, 678.6 cm^-1. 50-ST/BM shows all modes with decreased Bi2MoO6 intensities and peak broadening at 798 cm^-1 due to oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further confirm the formation of the composite, Raman experiment (Fig. 2A) was performed for the B i 2 M o O 6, s r T i O 3, and the 50-ST/BM nanocomposite.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bi2MoO6 shows Bi-O, Mo-O, Mo-O-Mo bands at 844, 798, 736, 605, 571 cm^-1. SrTiO3 shows Sr-O, Ti-O bands 850-500 cm^-1, prominent at 738 cm^-1. 50-ST/BM shows Sr-O, Ti-O, MoO6 bonds with 844 cm^-1 band shifted indicating strong interactions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FTIR spectra for pure B i 2 M o O 6, s r T i O 3, and the 50-ST/BM nanocomposite are presented in Fig. 2(B).

nodes.characterization_summary: 50-ST/BM shows Ti^4+ (Ti 2p3/2 458.49 eV, 2p1/2 464.17 eV), Bi^3+ (Bi 4f7/2 159.35 eV, 4f5/2 164.3 eV), Mo^6+ (Mo 3d 231.31, 234.51 eV) and Mo^4+ (232.53, 236.59 eV), Sr^2+ (Sr 3d5/2 132.8 eV, 3d3/2 134.5 eV), O 1s lattice oxygen (529.88 eV), oxygen vacancies (530.47 eV), surface oxygen (532.01 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ti 2p peaks are well deconvoluted into two peaks as Ti 2 p 1/2 (464.17), and Ti 2 p 3/2 (458.49), which exhibit the existence of T i 4+ atom... The O 1 s spectrum of the 50-ST/BM composite is divided into three distinct peaks... located at binding energies of 529.88, 530.47, and 532.01 eV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bandgaps: SrTiO3 3.2 eV, Bi2MoO6 2.70 eV, 50-ST/BM 2.94 eV. Heterojunction shows enhanced visible light absorption vs pure SrTiO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The bandgap of the S r T i O 3, 90-ST/BM, 70-ST/BM, 50-ST/BM, 30-ST/BM, 10-ST/BM, and B i 2 M o O 6 catalysts was found to be 3.2 eV, 3.16 eV, 3.10 eV, 2.94 eV, 2.89 eV, 2.72 eV and 2.70 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: SrTiO3 shows 3D nanocubes 30-50 nm. Bi2MoO6 shows nanoflakes. Composites show cubes intercalated on nanoflakes with merging of shapes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further examine the morphology of the prepared samples HRSEM analysis was performed.
The HRTEM image of 50-ST/BM is shown in Fig. 5(H), which effectively illustrates the formation of heterojunctions.

nodes.characterization_summary: 50-ST/BM EDS confirms presence of Sr, Ti, Bi, Mo, O elements uniformly distributed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 6 (A and B) illustrates the elemental mapping and EDS of 50-ST/BM.

nodes.characterization_summary: 50-ST/BM shows lowest PL intensity indicating reduced exciton recombination compared to bare SrTiO3 and Bi2MoO6.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The excitons recombination in the catalysts was investigated by the photoluminescence (PL) spectra and the spectra are shown in Fig. 10A.

nodes.characterization_summary: 50-ST/BM shows significantly decreased impedance indicating improved charge carrier diffusion compared to bare materials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nyquist plots from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) were used to assess the charge carrier migration and diffusion at the interface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Flat band potentials vs NHE: SrTiO3 -0.53 V, Bi2MoO6 -0.70 V, 50-ST/BM -0.57 V. Donor densities: SrTiO3 3.97×10^18 cm^-3, Bi2MoO6 3.11×10^21 cm^-3, 50-ST/BM 2.02×10^20 cm^-3. Positive slopes confirm n-type semiconductors.
